title: Counting what a lamp illuminates
bodyMd:
A town replaced its street lamps with brighter fixtures and later recorded more reports of damaged bicycles. Some residents concluded that the new lighting had encouraged vandalism. A council analyst suggested that better illumination might instead have made existing damage easier to notice. Reports were a product not only of damage but also of detection and willingness to contact the council.

The analyst recommended inspecting a fixed sample of bicycle racks at regular intervals, using the same inspection procedure before and after lighting changes. She also proposed recording foot traffic, because more people passing the racks could affect both damage and reporting. The proposal did not assume that lighting was harmless. It aimed to separate several pathways through which the same intervention could alter the number appearing in the council's complaint register.
